questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was a German speaking area, and that the relevant faculty of the university was comparable or higher than that of my home university. Additionally, that the opportunity was available to take language courses if I found it necessary. Lastly, that the city but also the country as a whole was safe and accessible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, since the exchange university provided many details and links to help me prepare my self as much as possible to the challenges that could face me when I arrived. Furthermore, they informed me of the duties I had when I arrived in regards to providing information to the city office and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any direct assistance, but I'm sure it could have been provided if I found it necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find housing, you must just send applications as early as possible and to as many places as possible. It is a great idea to search around on the internet for possible places to stay, as there are many student houses though out the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have to find the relevant websites your self, but otherwise it is pretty straightforward. There are many places to apply for. Depending on where they are, they might even be closer to the university than the housing opportunities provided by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to fill out informations on mobility online, and attach relevant documents, but otherwise it was pretty simple. At one point a Learning Agreement had to be provided, but here one should just use the template provided by the host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I'm sure the relevant help was available if I found it necessary.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful in registering for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have your documents in order, since some of them will be provided to you in a physical format. Otherwise, just be diligent and double check everything has been done.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of the courses may seem higher than that of the home institution due to a more old school way of teaching. This is evident when it comes to the examination, where in most cases no previous exams are provided to practice on. Sometimes the solutions to the problem sets will also not be provided, which means that it is vital that one show up for the TA-sessions.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, at points the teaching style could come across as more old fashioned, but that said, everyone was always very kind and helpfull if I had any questions. It is just on the student to ask the questions to achieve the highest learning outcome.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Normative Economics, Financial Crises, Advanced Corporate Finance, Econometrics for Development Economists, Stress Testing of Banks, Bank Treasury Management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Normative Economics, Financial Crises, Advanced Corporate Finance, Econometrics for Development Economists, Stress Testing of Banks

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was a bit more expensive than I had imagined, which is to say that it is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For sport activities there is ASVZ where, either for free or a small fee, it is possible to participate in around 130 different sporting activities. There are plenty of cultural events around the city, where many of them are for free as a student. For social activities, the ESN organises several events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Even though I did not myself participate in them, I have heard many good things about the ESN events, which many exchange students participate in during the first weeks of the exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is an endless array of hiking opportunities, many of which I used myself. Otherwise the city is full of music events, many of which are classical and free for students. Visiting the other large cities is also really fun, alongside skiing, and lastly going to see an ice hockey match is a great experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough, since the differences are relatively minor.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Swiss people are very kind and open, so don't be afraid to talk to them, especially those who you have courses with. That way you will build a connection when you talk with the week after week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging apart from the language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The orderliness, punctuality and calmness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Even if you want academically challenging courses, remember that you are on exchange and that you most likely also want to experience other things too, and thus it can be difficult to excel academically while taking time off to enjoy other sides of the country. Say yes to every opportunity you get offered for activities. Enjoy it, since the time flies.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: For public transport, but the Half Fare Card, since that will cut fares by 50%. Think about whether it makes sense to open a bank account to save money. Read as many things as you can to be as prepared as possible to when you first get there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet and socialise with swiss people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
